text.p: Leading Latvian bank Pareks Bank is expecting to get a Standard & Poor's credit rating by the start of the summer, bank deputy president Viktor Krasovitsky told Dienas Bizness newspapaper on Tuesday.
"Latvia was given a high credit rating so we will try to make sure that the one given to the bank will not be lower," Krasovitsky told the newspaper.
He said the slide in the bank's first quarter profit was explained by the fact it transferred a part of its profit into reserves to achieve as high a rating as possible.
The bank reported a first quarter profit of 691,000 lats.
Krasovitsky also said the bank would wait until next year before applying for a Thomson BankWatch rating as it could not get one higher than awarded to Latvia by Thomson, BBB-.
"This rating was not high as the experts based it on 1995 figures," he said, noting it would wait until the agency increased its sovereign rating for Latvia.
Krasovitsky also did not rule out the possibility of Pareks becoming a public company but it would not do this for the timebeing.
"It would not be logical to sell a highly profitable business which gives 80 to 100 percent in dividends," Krasovitsky said.
To determine the market value of the bank's shares it has considered the possibility of quoting a small part of its stock on Western stock exchanges.
